## Prepared local boundary

The existing harness still starts its pinned owned PostgreSQL and actual private mutual-TLS Temporal Server, builds a fresh worker image and runs the actual production entrypoint as UID 10001 with its existing read-only filesystem, dropped capabilities, private credential volumes and bounded resources. No replacement activity, TLS bypass, world-readable key, privileged container, provider credential or default API is introduced.

After the original authenticated operation, outage/recovery and operator-pause checks, the new check installs a bounded schema-table lock in the disposable platform database, then triggers the owned sweep. A fresh PostgreSQL connection must observe the exact schema-read query blocked by the run-owned lock session, scoped to the original worker container address. Temporal must independently describe a RUNNING owned sweep with exactly one STARTED `sweepReconcilePass` activity, attempt 1, maximum attempts 1 and the original worker identity.

The harness then delivers SIGTERM to that original worker. It requires the worker's drain marker before another authenticated description confirms the same still-started activity. Another fresh PostgreSQL observer must see the same waiter and blocker with a different observer PID. An idle, merely scheduled, completed, retried or substituted activity cannot satisfy this check. The original worker must then exit 0 without OOM or SIGKILL and record its stopped marker without secret output. The blocker always finishes its bounded rollback before recovery or existing owned-resource cleanup proceeds.

This is a hold at read-only schema prerequisites, before controller lease acquisition or provider mutation admission. PostgreSQL exposes no Temporal task identifier for that connection: the evidence proves the concurrent started sweep and exact schema waiter on the same worker, and explicitly leaves SQL-to-specific-activity attribution unproved. The production five-second lock timeout remains intact. If image-local SDK startup or scheduling misses the held interval, the attempt fails; an earlier successful observation cannot rescue it.

A distinct worker container and identity then use the same image, stores, namespace, TLS material and actual entrypoint. Authenticated retained history for the original pinned workflow/run/activity must show exactly one scheduled, started and completed activity; matching event links; maximum attempts 1; the original worker as both starter and completer; and the existing `deferred/prerequisites_unavailable` result. Failed, timed-out, cancelled or retried histories refuse. The fresh worker must restore actual readiness and produce a different current successful sweep. The separate existing idle SIGTERM drain is retained on this recovery worker.

Independent SQL connections before shutdown, after drain and after recovery hash the complete existing failed signed-read operation and confirm empty consumed-approval, CodeBuild-launch and authenticated-agent-receipt inventories. The snapshots must match and use distinct observer PIDs. These empty inventories cannot establish preservation of a used approval or recovery of an accepted effect receipt; nonempty inventories refuse rather than borrowing mutation evidence. No authority, approval, receipt or fence row is rewritten by the new probe.

## Evidence and remaining work

New safety cases cover scalar admission, wrong identities and activity states, retry/event-link refusals, private-output projection, exact SQL observer scope, authority snapshot changes and source ordering around SIGTERM and the distinct recovery entrypoint. They are source/scalar models, are unrun, and cannot prove actual SDK history, Linux signals, SQL locks, TLS, image provenance or cleanup. Existing tests and their original cases remain present.

The new `inFlightShutdown` evidence keeps its scope explicit and sets provider mutation acceptance, consumed-approval preservation, effect-receipt recovery and SQL-to-activity attribution to false. The original read remains an expected no-target refusal. Full accepted-provider-mutation shutdown/cancellation, uncertain-write recovery without blind replay, consumed browser approval, nonempty durable receipts and database-fence behavior remain outstanding. Those may require the default API/browser approval and separately authorized live accounts; they are outside this local source delta.
